newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial conduct guidelines cost the job of another Government frontbencher yesterday and three other Ministers are under pressure because of their ownership of shares, including Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer, Finance Mnister John Fahey and Industry Minister John Moore. Page 1.

Netscape Communications will today unveil its latest weapon in the battle to win the biggest share of the corporate Internet market, a A$106 software package called Communicator which allows people to send electronic mail, access the Internet and work colaboratively. Page 1.

The Federal Government has set up a major review of the Australian Defence Force's A$5 billion annual non-combat budget. The move comes at the same time as a A$280 million three-year restructuring plan of the ADF which will further strengthen combat unit in Queensland and Western Australia. Page 3.

After a vote narrowly upheld the Government's new regulations for woodchip exports, seven Coalition Senators were forced to reveal they had shareholdings in logging firms. The support of Senator Brian Harradine and Senator Mal Colston allowed the 20 per cent increase in woodchip exports to 6.25 million tonnes. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the resignation of a second senior Government figure in three days for a breach of the ministerial code of conduct - Senator Brian Gibson has joined Senator Jim Short on the backbench - and amid calls from the Opposition for a third resignation, that of Industry Minister John Moore, Prime Minister John Howard has been forced to review the code. Page 1.

Amid national outrage at the theft of 130 million-year-old stegosaurus tracks in Western Australia, eminent palaeontologist Dr Tony Thulborn warned last night that dinosaur fossil sites were being targeted by organised gangs, telling The Australian the stgosaurus theft was the "latest in a long line" of thefts from prime scientific sites. Page 1.

Responding to a question form Liberal backbencher Brendan Nelson yesterday, Prime Minister John Howard said he is prepared to negotiate the terms of a bipartisan motion against racial discrimination, but said he could not support all the areas contained in the Opposition's proposed motion. Page 3.

As Bob Mansfield, the businessman appointed to review the ABC, winds up a series of interviews he is conducting as part of his inquiry into the ABC's charter, he has given the national broadcaster strong support against claims of bias in news coverage, saing he would take no role which would "decimate" it. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following the resignation of Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasurer Brian Gibson in circumstances almost identical to those which resulted in Assistant Treasurer Jim Short resigning on Sunday, Prime Minister John Howard has signalled changes to his miniterial code, suggesting the system is unfair to frontbenchers who own shares as opposed to other investments. Page 1.

In an unusual break with the tradition of Governments not commenting on Royal Commissions during the course of their hearings, Carr Government MPs at a Labor right-wing Caucus meeting, and the subsequent full Caucus meeting, accused the Police Royal Commision yesterday of protecting senior judges and lawyers from public exposure of paedophilia activities. Page 1.

Under a major overhaul of the family law system announced by Attorney-General Daryl Williams yesterday, divorce settlements between couples planning to marry will be legalised and future superannuation payouts will be treated as property to be divided between divorcing partners. Page 1.

Just a day after Prime Minister John Howard said he believed there was no evidence there was any national debate on race, he has bowed to heightening political pressure to deal with growing divisions on race relations, agreeing yesterday to negotiate a biartisan statement rejecting racial discrimination and intolerance. Page 1.
THE AGE

Following the resignation of Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasurer Brian Gibson, who quit after finding he had made a decision earlier this year affecting a company in the Boral Group in which he had a shareholding, and amid growing pressure on other Mnisters, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday foreshadowed a change in his ministerial code of conduct. Page 1.

The Age has discovered Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer had investments, of an unspecified value, in some of Australia's largest companies, including BHP, Western Mining, Qantas and TNT, as recently as two months ago. Fischer told the House of Representatives he had disposed of the shares one day after Assistant Treasurer Jim Short resigned. Page 1.

The Austin and Repatriation Medical Centre last night confirmed 19 per cent, or one in five patients, in the busy surgical unit were infected by an outbreak of potentially lethal methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in March. The infection was tracd to dirty metal retractors used to keep patients' chests open during surgery. Page 1.

On the second day of a coronial inquest into the deaths of nine people who died during a fire at Kew Cottages, the Department of Human Services yesterday rejected suggestions that firefighters received misleading information from Kew staff about the number of people evacuated during the fire. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
